measured_by: measure_realtime_transparent_tint_spread.py: EEVEE 5.2.2, 64 by 64 frame, 16 samples, the 9 by 9 patch mean, over 8 shifts of the whole scene along y (k * 0.0001, k = 1..8). Each shift is an independent realisation of EEVEE's dither noise.

BLENDED.derivation: EEVEE's value is the same at every shift (sigma 0). The EXR is half-float; for values in [0.5, 1) the rounding error is at most 2^-12 = 0.000244140625. The test asserts Potter against this mean with that bound alone.

MIX.derivation: A Mix Shader at Fac 0.5 of the Transparent pane (Color TINT) and an opaque black Principled, rendered BLENDED. The opaque closure passes nothing, so EEVEE sums the transmittance to 0.5 * TINT (`eevee_nodetree_lib.bsl.hh`, closure_eval(ClosureTransparency), weighted by the closure weights), and the pane shows that over the radiance-1 backdrop: (0.1, 0.4, 0.2). EEVEE's value is the same at every one of the 8 shifts (sigma 0). The half-float rounding bound of the EXR for these values is at most 2^-13; the test uses 2^-12, the bound BLENDED uses, as a margin. Potter's weighted sum (`render/scene.rs` surface_tint) gives the same 0.5 * TINT by hand (`weighted_tint` tests).

DITHERED.runtime_assertion: BLENDED and MIX are asserted against their measured patch means within each method's tolerance. DITHERED is printed as a diagnostic beside the same-build 64x64, 16-sample source render with seed 0 (Metal fast-math dither hash), not asserted. The mean over independent y-shifts remains diagnostic, not the per-frame reference.
DITHERED.mechanism: EEVEE 5.2.2's depth prepass discards a fragment when average(g_transmittance) > alpha_threshold. The threshold uses primitive-interpolated world P, max(length(dFdx(P)), length(dFdy(P))), log-discretized Wyman-McGuire 3D hashes, a CDF interpolation, and a base-7 Halton jitter at sample+1 (`eevee_surf_depth.bsl.hh`, `eevee_transparency.bsl.hh`, `eevee_sampling.cc`). Final renders use alpha_hash_scale 0.1 (`eevee_pipeline.cc`); the film then accumulates kept samples with its source filter.
